comparison: Both address SIRT2-mediated deacetylation of ACSS2 under amino acid stress (C24-C34). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging experimental approaches, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting 'some evidence supporting these findings is incomplete' and requesting 'direct demonstration of target deacetylation by sirtuin 2.' This represents a significant disagreement on evidence sufficiency.

Both address K271 identification as the SIRT2 deacetylation site (C46-C50). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a strength, noting 'Identification of a novel acetylation site on ACSS2' and recognizing the mass spectrometry and mutational analysis as solid evidence. Strong agreement.

Both address SIRT2 regulation of ACSS2 at the protein level (C35-C40). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED through protein stability assays and mRNA analysis, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting 'data for this manuscript seems preliminary as nearly all data is performed in one cell line' and requesting validation across multiple systems. Disagreement on generalizability.

Both address proteasomal degradation mechanism (C41-C45). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Reviewers acknowledge 'solid data showing ACSS2 acetylation can be regulated by targeting SIRT2 and that SIRT2 regulates ACSS2 ubiquitination.' Strong agreement on this mechanistic finding.

Both address the mechanistic link between K271 deacetylation and ubiquitination (C51-C55, with OpenEval also including C4-C5). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Reviewers recognize 'acetylation of 271 protects ACSS2 from proteasomal degradation in a SIRT2-dependent manner' as a key finding. Strong agreement.

Both address functional consequences in lipogenesis and adipocyte differentiation (C58-C63, with OpenEval also including C6-C7). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting 'overall role of ACSS2 K271 acetylation is not well characterized' and suggesting isotope tracing would better validate functional impact. Disagreement on functional validation sufficiency.

Both address the overall regulatory model (C64-C66, C69, with peer review also including C3-C7). OpenEval finds the core mechanism SUPPORTED while noting C66 is speculative. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, stating 'further support is required for the model put forward by the authors' and raising statistical concerns. Disagreement on model validation, with peer review expressing broader concerns about the overall framework.

Both address citation-based background claims about DNL and disease relevance (C1, C8-C9, C70, C83, with peer review covering broader background C1-C23, C28, C33, C56-C57, C67-C68, C70-C75, C78, C81, C83). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. These established facts provide accepted context and show strong agreement.

OpenEval addresses ACSS2 background claims (C10-C16) as SUPPORTED through appropriate citations. Peer review groups these with other background claims (R8) and also rates them SUPPORTED as accepted knowledge. Agreement on background context.

OpenEval addresses acetylation regulation background (C17-C23) as SUPPORTED through citations. Peer review groups these with other background claims (R8) and rates them SUPPORTED. Agreement on established background.

OpenEval addresses SIRT2 stress-responsive background (C28, C33, C67-C68) as SUPPORTED through citations. Peer review groups these with other background claims (R8) and rates them SUPPORTED. Agreement on background context.

OpenEval addresses SIRT2's role in DNL regulation background (C71-C77) as SUPPORTED, with C76-C77 involving some inference. Peer review groups C71-C75 with background claims (R8, SUPPORTED) but places C76-C77 in interpretive claims (R9, UNCERTAIN). Partial disagreement on whether these claims are established facts versus interpretations.

OpenEval addresses contrast with SIRT1 work (C78-C80) as SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer review groups C79-C80 with interpretive claims (R9, UNCERTAIN) that extend beyond direct experimental data. Disagreement on whether the SIRT1/SIRT2 distinction is sufficiently validated.

OpenEval addresses amino acid stress and lipid metabolism context (C81-C82) as SUPPORTED through citations. Peer review groups C82 with interpretive claims (R9, UNCERTAIN). Minor disagreement on whether this represents established context versus speculative connection.

Both address therapeutic implications (C84). Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes no therapeutic interventions were tested, while peer reviewers acknowledge the speculative nature of therapeutic claims. Strong agreement on the preliminary nature of therapeutic implications.

OpenEval addresses biochemical and genetic background (C2, C56-C57) as SUPPORTED through general knowledge and citations. Peer review groups these with background claims (R8) and rates them SUPPORTED. Agreement on established background.
